messages.subject: Change in usermodel breaks models that previously ran without issues
messages.subject_clean: Change in usermodel breaks models that previously ran without issues
messages.body_plain:
I updated the package last week and suddenly models that ran without issues previously now no longer converge. I've encountered issues with 3 unrelated models now (in 2 different datasets) and I don't see why these in particular would suddenly not converge. I think the recent update in usermodel is causing the trouble. Did some default behaviors change? I'd be happy to use an old version but I can't find previous code releases.
reposted github issue #86

messages.subject_clean: Change in usermodel breaks models that previously ran without issues
messages.body_plain:
Hi Joelle,

Thanks for raising this. There was a recent change to the GenomicSEM code to mirror updates to the lavaan package, so as you say if these models converged before there's something about this update that is causing them not to converge. It's unclear right now if it's a bug or something about the recent updates related to how model convergence is evaluated in lavaan that is causing this issue you are observing. To help tease this apart it would be helpful to see the code you ran and the error you got for one model as I'm still able to run different forms of models in different datasets on my end and so can't seem to find something that is breaking with the new update to troubleshoot.

Best,
  Andrew

Thanks for the quick reply. This is one of the models that ran before but now doesn’t converge:

If you want to do some digging I can share the results and/or covariance matrix via e-mail.

Cheers,

Joëlle

messages.body_plain:
Hi Joëlle,

This likely won't fix your issue, but just to simplify things the model syntax below should be equivalent to what you've written above if you use the std.lv <http://std.lv> = TRUE argument when running the model. If factors are outcomes then the default is to correlate them unless they load on the same factor, so fixing those factor correlations aren't necessary.

"G =~ F1 + F2 + F3 + F4

F1 =~ SMKCES + PACKYE + SMKDEP + ALCDEP + ALCFRQ + COCDEP + CANEV + SMKINI + SMKAGE

F2 =~ CANDEP + COCDEP + OPIODEP + SMKAGE

F3 =~ ALCDEP + ALCCON + ALCFRQ + ALCP

F4 =~ CANEV + CANFL + SMKINI"

I tried running a similar model with psychiatric data I have on hand as below and am getting output without issues. I think this tells us that this model specification is more generally fine, but is causing issues applied to your particular dataset.

BaseModel<-"F1=~AN+OCD+TS
F2=~SCZ+BIP+ALCH
F3=~PTSD+ADHD+ALCH+MDD+TS+ASD
F4=~PTSD+MDD+ANX+ALCH
G =~ F1 + F2 + F3 + F4"
usermodel(covstruc=LDSC_P,model=BaseModel,std.lv <http://std.lv>=TRUE)

My current sense is that this is specific to your data/model and not a recently introduced bug in the Genomic SEM code, but rather something about the lavaan update that is causing the model not to converge. What is the specific warning you are getting? Just that it didn't converge?

There's nothing in the description of the recent lavaan update that tells me why your model would stop converging (https://lavaan.ugent.be/history/dot6.html). You could try reverting to an older version of lavaan to see if that fixes things.

Best,

  Andrew

messages.body_plain:
Thanks Andrew, I think it's not unlikely that the issues are caused by lavaan setting stricter limits for convergence, because I only encounter this issue for models that were already quite unstable.

In the meantime, I have been able to fix things by reverting back to the old versions of lavaan and GenomicSEM. I tried different commits, this combination worked:

devtools::install_github("GenomicSEM/GenomicSEM@4650dec90fce9985d566b8a5f9ff89abd6762632")
devtools::install_version("lavaan", version = "0.6-18", repos = "http://cran.us.r-project.org")

messages.subject: userGWAS: warning "some estimated ov variances are negative", NA Qsnp
messages.subject_clean: userGWAS: warning "some estimated ov variances are negative", NA Qsnp
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

After getting a model with good fit for a second-order model, I ran userGWAS on the model. I encounter 2 issues that I really appreciate your insights.

All the SNPs have "some estimated ov variances are negative" warning, resulting from GWAS of the latent factors. Furthermore, for the second-order latent factor, every Qsnp is NA, and hence without Qsnp p-value.

This is my model:
"
F1 =~ T1 + T2 + T3 + T4 + T5
F2 =~ F1 + T6 + T7 + T8 + T9
F1 ~ SNP
F2 ~ SNP
"
The model fit statistics are chisq(df=27) = 454.8504, AIC = 490, CFI = 0.977, SRMR = 0.057.
None of the standardized factor loadings exceeds 1, and none of the standardized SE is negative. Hence, I didn't apply any constraints.
Upon inspection of the estimated variance for every trait for all SNPs, all of the estimated variance, for example T1~~T1, is positive.

Thank you in advance for the help!

Best regards,
Thanh Le

messages.subject_clean: Runtime for multivariate GWAS with large number of traits and SNPs
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I would appreciate for your help with the following issue I have,

I am interested in conducting multivariate GWAS with 11 clinical traits that are genetically correlated among each other. The individual GWAS summary statistics for these 11 traits contains ~30 million SNPs. Therefore, it seems like running userGWAS might take unrealistically long time.

Do you have any suggestions on how to proceed with such data?

My model specification is as follows,

model<-"F1 =~ trait 1 + trait 2 + trait 3 + trait 4 + trait 5

F2 =~ trait 6 + trait 7  + trait 8 + trait 9 + trait 10 + trait 11

F1~~F2

F1 ~ SNP

F2 ~ SNP"

best wishes,

Pashupati
